output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is almost certainly caused by Finance's 14 April change (FC-0417). It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger cases to the Billing Resolution team. Billing referrals went from 7% to 54% of billing calls in the same week. Referred calls resolve only about 34% of the time, against 82% for the rest. Customers then call back to ask about their referral. Referral rates are the same for new and experienced agents (56%, 54%, 53%), and experienced agents' FCR fell by the same amount. So the April intake, the tariff rise and the IVR change are not the main cause. Tariff enquiries resolve as well as before. I haven't checked workload, but the pattern doesn't fit it. Don't put the April intake on performance plans. That would punish the wrong group. Instead, agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling of credits, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Finance has said it would consider this. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. I'm fairly confident, though I haven't confirmed that the tariff rise has no effect.
